question: The graph, \(G,\) of \(y=\log_{10}x\) is rotated \(90^\circ\) counter-clockwise about the origin to obtain a new graph \(G'.\) Which of the following is an equation for \(G'?\)
solution:
Track an arbitrary point so that the rotation determines the equation of the whole graph. A \(90^\circ\) counterclockwise rotation about the origin sends \((u,v)\) to \((-v,u)\): the positive horizontal direction turns upward, and the positive vertical direction turns left.

Let \((u,v)\) lie on \(G\), so \(u>0\) and \(v=\log_{10}u\). Its rotated coordinates satisfy \(x=-v\) and \(y=u\). Therefore
\[
-x=\log_{10}y,
\]
which, by the definition of a logarithm, is equivalent to
\[
y=10^{-x}.
\]
Conversely, for every real \(x\), the value \(y=10^{-x}\) is positive and \((y,-x)\) lies on \(G\). Rotating that point gives \((x,y)\), so the equation describes all of \(G'\). The answer is \(\boxed{y=10^{-x}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
